label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Skier Triggered Release
reports.comment: quick: When traversing a slope to avoid another party, we triggered a size 1-2. Slow moving due to lower slope angle, but certainly a wakeup call about how weak some near-ground layers are.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Variable conditions with lots of recent wind effect. Found poor conditions and wind slab closer to Peyto lake (nice photo though!), but further south on the eastern aspect at treeline and below we found some really nice snow in the thin trees and open chutes. Did a few laps and had a good day overall despite the wind. A size 1 skier triggered avalanche occurred on a convex roll moments befo…

reports.title: Early season rockies conditions east side of the 93n
reports.comment: quick: Left the car by the weather station south of bowsummit at 8:45 hs was 15cm but supportive at roadside and quickly turned into 25-40cm as we started going up. Temp was -6 and winds were light from the N, sky was broken but clouds were thin and wispy. At 2390m we would go through pockets of 25-60cm. used the w-sw aspect to ascend observation sub peak west ridge. lots of thick to thin issues w…

reports.title: Observation sub peak bowl
reports.comment: quick: Skied the bowl below Observation sub peak. HS was 70-90cm at 2550m on a sheltered WNW aspect. We did two ECT tests but didn't see any propagation. There was 10-20cm of new snow, however it was quite heavy and/or wind pressed, so the skiing was just ok. The snowpack was very low (20-25cm) down below treeline which made travel quite 'sporty'.

reports.title: Avalanche Involvement
reports.comment: incident: Parks Canada responded to an InReach activation for three skiiers who were hit by a natural avalanche in a couloir on the east ridge of Mt. Patterson. There were no burials, but all three went for a ~100m tumble sustaining various injuries, the worst being a head injury and broken ribs. Gear was lost and all three were evacuated to a waiting ambulance. The avalanche appeared to be a loos…

reports.title: Bow summit
reports.comment: snowpack: Good skiing at bow summit in a narrow band at the top of treeline.  Everything else on the 93N looked like a tough approach. Skiing was good in the open but the snowpack had faceted out around small trees.   We found isolated windslabs on NE aspect sitting on a facet layer at treeline.

reports.title: Poking our heads out there
reports.comment: quick: Great skiing to be had in the alpine. Found some isolated windslabs in the inmediate lees of convexities and ridges. Average HS of 100cms in the alpine, where we were skiing. Found 10-15 cms of facets off the ground, to a highly variable melt freeze crust most likely from early October. 20 cms of smaller facets above the crust in some places. In places there was up to 70 cms of settled stor…

reports.title: Snow observations, Bow Summit area
reports.comment: snowpack: Good skiing conditions with new snow over a firm base but lots of whumpfing on the Oct 26 crust in areas travelled today.

reports.title: Flower Coulior
reports.comment: quick: Climbed and skied Flower Couloir and the bowl above. Some fresh snow over the past few days made for generally good ski quality. Very little recent wind effect. Did 2 tests below the Flower Couloir at ~2400m NE aspect, HS110cm - CTH24 - non planar break ~30cm down on crust for both tests. I absolutely wailed on the remainder and took extreme force to trigger the depth hoar surprisingly. Dec…

reports.title: Bow summit couloir
reports.comment: incident: Skier accidental triggered underfoot on decent. 10-15cm of storm slab, size 1.

reports.title: Unnamed Ramp
reports.comment: quick: HS of 60-90cms with some wind effect in the drainage. 35cm overlies the late October crust and was supportive to skiers. Cool temps to -11 deg in the morning and -5 deg in pm and excellent ski quality. Some evidence of couple old Na activity to size 2 out of steep unsupported lee features at ridgetop but no new in our travels today. Hard SC CT results below the crust in facet’s size 2. Mod …

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak Area
reports.comment: quick: Ski toured up the western slopes facing the highway near Observation  Sub Peak today.  Sunny skies and cool temps (-17 to -9 celcius) all day.  On the way down, near ridgetop, a size 2 slab avalanche was remotely triggered while cutting back on a low angle slope to the shoulder.  Moderate winds all day were transporting the recent storm snow and a significant amount of cross-loading was obs…

reports.title: Observation sub peak
reports.comment: quick: Observed wind slabs in N chute on Cirque forepeak and one whumpf. The ridge to Observation subpeak had cornices and loaded pokets at immediate lee.  One wind slab broke off about 30m deep and 3 meter long but didn't slide. In lower alpine over convex roll triggered size 1.5ish remotely by ski cut (broke off 5 m below me) 50cm deep vert soft storm slab on very hard sun crust. Ran about 50m i…

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: 5cm low-density snow overlying mfCr BTL and in sheltered areas above TL. Evidence of recent L-M SW'erly winds, resulting in wind affected snow above TL and formation of windslab on lee slopes. Observed 2 recent (last 24hrs) Na windslabs, 20-30cm deep on NE asp. sz 1 at 2400m, and sz 2 at 2600m in the steep immediate lee of ridge crest. We stuck to supported terrain on our descent and had re…

reports.title: Bow summit CT
reports.comment: quick: Dug a pit at the end / 3rd nub at Bow Summit. No results on CT. Even when putting body weight on the column post CT only top layers giving in to weight no failure below. Around 30cm newer snow sitting a top a few harder crust layers (around 35cm deep to ground). Around 4 layers hardening with small softer sections between - maybe consolidating? No expert though. First layer softer, bottom 3…

reports.title: Wapta Ramp above Bow Hut
reports.comment:
quick: Conditions varied from light powder to wind affected. Generally good skiing, especially off of Mount Gordon and the Wapta Ramp. We dug a test pit on the way up. CT-N.

Test pit was at 2500m, 28 degrees, NE aspect. Air temp was -9 degrees, snow depth 135cm.

reports.title: Observation Sub-Peak profile
reports.comment: quick: Profile from treeline on the east side of Observation Peak.

reports.title: Crowfoot area
reports.comment: quick: Sign if a recent soft storm slab release below cliff face. Looks like it was triggered by cornice colapse or higher sluffing. It ran 150 meters down gully. Ski cuts on convexities had no results and while boot packing variable crust layers were found but overall snowpack felt solid.

reports.title: Jimmy Simpson Jr
reports.comment: quick: Great conditions on Jimmy Jr today. Clear skies with a -23c start! ~15cm of new snow on a supportive crust made for easy travel. A bit of surface hoar was forming but seemed to bake off from the sun. Did 2 tests at ~2350m SE before the first steep roll. HS 80cm -CTH27 uneven break and CTH24 uneven break - both 35cm down on crust. My partner got CTN. His HS was 130cm. We noted no signs of in…

reports.title: Mosquito sub peak
reports.comment: quick: Decent ski quality up high. Mixture of wind crust and soft snow in the alpine. Good snow at tree line. Shallow snow pack and full of land sharks BTL. Day started very cold but warmed up and was sunny. Snow started to snow ball by late afternoon on the S.W. slopes.

reports.title: Dolomite Circuit
reports.comment:
quick: Skied the Dolomite Circuit from West to East (clockwise) today. Easy travel along a skin track highway up to Katherine Ridge. The East slopes of Katherine Ridge had a fairly supportive windcrust, with faceting taking place from ground up - approximately 40cm deep. No real interface for instability at this point.
Once we moved into the undulating North slopes of Dolomite Peak, we experience …

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak
reports.comment: quick: Made the summit of Observation south peak via the drainage closest to Cirque Peak. Alpine was severely wind effected, and the wind picked up throughout the day today - blowing eastward - moderate winds with strong gusts in the alpine above 2600m. The southern aspect was blown nearly bare up here, with settled shallow wind slab. We avoided venturing onto E aspect beyond the SE aspect, since …

reports.title: Hellen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Good ski quality on Hellen Shoulder on E/SE aspects.  120 cm snow depth around TL but highly variable below.  There is an impressive new slide path on the summer trail approach which wasn’t here last year (see photo).  SW to W aspects had a mix of sun crust and wind slab so we avoided these. NE-E aspects skied better (20 cm ski pen) but got more faceted and bottomless in denser trees.  Lots…

reports.title: Jimmy Junior
reports.comment: quick: Beautiful day on the Icefields Parkway. Jimmy Junior conditions have been altered significantly from last weekends report as a result of a wind event mid week. Skiied mellow slopes underneath first cliff band - wind slab was touchy in areas that had not been impacted by the sun as of 1pm.

reports.title: Cirque fore-peak
reports.comment: quick: Skied the west slopes below cirque sub-peak. Avoided the high alpine assuming wind slabs, but found good powder from around 100m above treeline all the way to the highway. Found so signs of instability or avalanches. South aspects at the edge of gullies had a very shallow snowpack (5-10cm, presumably wind-blown). It would be nice to see the snowpack 30-50cm deeper as there’s still a few lan…

reports.title: Flower couloir and another to the lookers L
reports.comment: quick: Skied the flower couloir and another to the lookers left afterward. We started up the petals in the bowl above the flower couloir, but turned around due to a stiff, shallow snowpack with a weak faceted base. In the couloirs we encountered a well settled and relatively deep snowpack with little recent wind effect.

reports.title: Size 1 Soft Slab
reports.comment: avalanche: Skier triggered remote from above convex roll. No involvement. Soft slab turning to powder almost directly after release. Debris ran slow and stopped on mid fan. Ran off or near ground. Could not collect crystal info as there was hang fire.

reports.title: Crystal Ridge North
reports.comment: quick: Went up Crystal ridge (the northern part). Found faceted unconsolidated and unsupportive snow below treeline, made for tricky ascent when venturing off the old skin track. At treeline the new snow was promising for some good skiing, but degraded as I ascended further. A lot of recent wind effect in the alpine on the west aspect of crystal ridge. Some slabs more substantial than others, and …

reports.title: Skier remote size 2
reports.comment: quick: Remote triggered size 2 on a SE aspect at 2640m off Crystal ridge. Triggered from a protected rib 20m skier left of the fracture line. Slab dimensions: 30cm x 70m. P- windslab over facets.

reports.title: Avalanche incident
reports.comment: incident: A group of 2 ski tourers triggered a size 2 avalanche while up-tracking at approximately 2700m.  The avalanche was 80m wide, 20-40cm deep, and ran 250m.  It was a wind slab that dug down to the basal facet layer.  Both skiers were caught on the flank but were not buried.  They lost their ski equipment, and were picked up by helicopter with no injuries.

reports.title: Observation Subpeak size 1.5 avalanche
reports.comment: quick: Size 1.5 skier triggered avalanche on SW aspect of Observation Subpeak. Within 200m of skier triggered slide from Nov 7 2018.

reports.title: Crowfoot Mountain
reports.comment: quick: Toured up to Crowfoot mountain on Sunday. From the parking lot up to treeline everything was as expected, passable but thin coverage. The moraines were mostly windswept with a mix of hard crusts and the occassional small pocket of blown around powder. Not aweful skiing on the moraines,  but not good either. As we got on to the glacier we probed like crazy people, suspecting areas of thin co…

reports.title: Bow Summit Full Profile
reports.comment: quick: Full profile at Bow Summit Study Plot done by Parks Canada Visitor Safety

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Compression test easy resistant planar results down 40cm, but with low density snow above. The slab hadn't stiffened up enough just yet in this area.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: It is currently a delicate balance to find slopes steep enough that the skiing is enjoyable yet supported enough by slope structure and vegetation that it is safe to ski. Crowfoot glades has some of this terrain. / avalanche: Slab avalanche originating in non skiable terrain of the crowfoot headwall. This turned almost completely into spindrift by the bottom of the cliff / snowpack: Ski pen…

reports.title: Bow Summit - deep and unstable
reports.comment: quick: Deep fresh snow at bow summit. Unsupportive facets below about 50cm of new snow made trail breaking a chore. Tons of wind transport noted today with strong winds. Recent natural activity noted in several places. Snowpack test result was poor. 2275m - treeline - NE aspect - 28 degree slope. CTE2 sudden planar 50cm down AND sudden collapse 110cm down simultaneously. Skied mellow slopes at tre…

reports.title: Bow Summit Sz 1.5 skier triggered
reports.comment: avalanche: Sz 1.5 Skier triggered. Party of 5, previous skiers skied more southerly section of slope. Last skier wondered more north and triggered the slide. Near a covered rock trigger point. 2 other parties in the area. CT 12 on lower section of slope @ 23°,Stay safe out there.

reports.title: Cirque Peak Outlier
reports.comment: quick: We skied very conservatively, due to the recent snow in the Rockies. We expected widespread instabilities and saw the results of many size 2 avalanches on our drive home. On Cirque Peak outlier, we did not encounter whoomphing or shooting cracks. Wind slab was present near treeline but had 10cm of stormsnow on top. A quick treeline pit produced CT13/14 SC down 40 and a ECTN14. Interface bet…

reports.title: Bow Hut approach (canyon)
reports.comment: avalanche: Remote trigger on small slope lookers right of regular exit slope from the canyon.  Triggered as first skier approached the slope.  Turned around so condition of slopes  beyond canyon not known.  Some sluffing in the canyon, but thin cover of snow, so likely from previous day(s).

reports.title: Crystal Ridge Remote Trigger
reports.comment: quick: SW slope, at 2450 m, remote triggered by second skier rolling in early to the slope. Stepped down to base. Size 1.0

reports.title: Helen Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Sunny and -10C. Boot deep powder. No tracks or anyone above treeline. Little if any evidence of any avalanches around valley. Cornice triggered avalanches on E face of Cirque Peak S ridge. Many whumps in flats. Avoided convex slopes. Skied 3 laps on mellow E face of Helen Ridge.

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Skies dolomite shoulder December 27 on South aspect slopes. There were pockets of powder, but snow was wind affected and icy up top. There was a large cornice at the top of the shoulder overhanging the eastern slopes. No new avalanche activity was observed.

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Nice riding and climbing conditions Sunday. Weather was -10°C at lunch with scattered clouds. Dug a quick pit at 2200m. Slope 34°. SOUTH Aspect. HS = 68cm. Observed CT12 just below the storm snow (~20cm down on an uneven break) and CT16 (planar) about 2/3 of the way down (roughly 45-50cm depth).

reports.title: Treeline Test Profile Dolomite South Shoulder
reports.comment: snowpack: Quick Test Profile found moderate to hard shears down 85-90cm failing in the large basal facets below the December 10 interface

reports.title: Avalanche - Bow Summit Area
reports.comment: quick: We stuck to the lower ridge and loose upper treeline in the bow summit area. While skinning from one run to the next, we noticed what appeared to be a fresh (less than 24 hours) size 1.5 slide. The crown was directly below some exposed rock on a line not typically skied with little tracks to no tracks around, so we suspect it was a natural. It was difficult to tell from our view point if it…

reports.title: Helen Shoulder Glades
reports.comment: quick: Detoured from a Wapta trip today, did two laps on Helen Shoulder. The predicted storm was rolling in full force, mostly high winds but cloudy conditions and some snow falling already. Wind was having a rapid affect on the snow, creating a hard slabby surface layer. There was also intense wind transport happening on the ridge. We experienced some cracks and whumpfs on the second lap, mostly …

reports.title: West Nile glades
reports.comment: quick: Skied the 'West Nile' trees below Bow Peak between 2100-1850m. Snow depth was 160-180cm at 1950m. Stability was surprisingly good fine where we skied (no cracks, slabs, etc.) and that includes steeper parts that were pushing 30 degrees. We stayed far below the alpine bowls above, and did not attempt to ski any of the steeper convex rolls at treeline. We heard a couple of large whumps while …

reports.title: west nile
reports.comment: quick: still con,con,con. Avalanches occurring and moving fast. (bow lake area). Got RB5 SP down 60 on storm layer in open trees in forest. 5 value not spectacular but fast clean shear right off the block (SP) was alarming.

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak Glades
reports.comment: snowpack: See attached profile, sudden collapses on Dec 10 facet deep persistent layer just above Oct 26 temperature crust

reports.title: wind triggered avalanhes
reports.comment: avalanche: 4 avalanches in total: a size 2, a 2.5 and a 3.5 all on the same SW slope of Cirque sub peak as well as a size 3 on Jimmy Junior across the road.

reports.title: Natural avalanche report from public
reports.comment:
avalanche: Report from public. Witnessed Na triggered on lookers right side of Jimmy Jr and spilled into Jimmy Jr Bowl. 
Also witnessed 3 Na's likely triggered by winds on cirque forepeak. A size 2, 2.5 and 3.5. All failing within storm snow and then almost immediately stepping down to the deep persistent layer

reports.title: Bow Hut approach: skier accidental sz 2.0
reports.comment: quick: We had been skiing super conservatively, and I could see that the slope had previously released during the storm which gave me false confidence.  I pushed my line out a bit too far from the dense trees and triggered a slide high above me. It released on the HST interface, but stepped down to basal layers over rocky terrain. I stayed on the surface, no injuries.

reports.title: Snow Profiles Highway 93N
reports.comment: snowpack: Extensive wind affect at alpine, windslabs evident.  Compression Test Easy third hit sudden collapse (CTE3 SC) on facets and depth hoar down 75cm failing below 20-30cm of pencil hard slab at 2350m.  Potential for long propagations.

reports.title: Crowfoot Shoulder Chutes
reports.comment: quick: Had some good turns on the far side of Crowfoot Shoulder, didn't note any signs of instability while skiing or skinning throughout the day. Skied a mix of open tries, small pillows and small chutes. Saw lots of parties closer to the lake but set our own tracks and did not encounter anyone in the area we skied. / snowpack: Dug a pit at 2243m on an East aspect. HS was 250cm! likely some wind …

reports.title: Cirque sub crystal ridge conditions and avalanches observed
reports.comment: quick: Toured around cirque sub peak/Crystal ridge area yesterday. Started from the road in the open flats below the obs/cirque drainage, was - 18 at the car around 9:30am. Started up traversing a couple drainages over the gain the col between cirque sub and crystal ridge high point. Stopped in mellow alpine dug a quick pit, west aspect 2400m 15 degrees hs 135 temp - 4(very strong inversion with r…

reports.title: Cirque Forpeak Trees
reports.comment: quick: Skied the trees on cirque peak today. Got a look at the very large skier triggered slab in the alpine that is a few days old, but didn't see anything new for activity. We stayed at treeline and below treeline. Above treeline was very wind affected and ski quality degraded quickly. Snow was very supportive for skiing. Sunny and an inversion, so temperatures felt near zero and surface snow wa…

reports.title: Crowfoot area
reports.comment: quick: Skied crowfoot glades and the chutes. Tracked but some pockets of decent snow. The bowl west/NW of crowfoot glades has naturally slid at some point and propagated to the edge of the treed area.

reports.title: Dolomite Peak South Ridge  Remotely-Triggered Avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: Today (Jan. 20) our party of 4 witnessed a size 2 avalanche which was remotely triggered by a party skiing near us.  There were no involvements and no burials.  The slide occurred at 2200m on a SE facing slope near the lower reaches of Dolomite Peak's south ridge.  While skinning up from app. 200m away, we saw a party of 2 approaching the slope from above.  The fracture started when the…

reports.title: Size 2 above mosquito creek toward Dolomites e
reports.comment:
avalanche: We did not see it. Although there were ski tracks above the start zone there was no tracks leading into the slide. So although I put it was a natural trigger it could still have been triggered by a skier. 
We checked the slide for signals and received none and saw two other skiers later on.

reports.title: Crowfoot Area
reports.comment:
quick: The day started off around zero degrees, calm, and partly cloudy. After some skiing, we hopped up a into the alpine from the south. The area was completely wind affected. Temperatures rose to 2 degrees and wind shifted/ picked up and was blowing strongly south for the afternoon. Was worried my doors were going to blow off when finishing up at the road. 

Skiing was ok. Last weekend, the sno…

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Skied a lap on Dolomite Shoulder from 2650m. 5-10cm of new snow sitting over the old tracked out, wind hammered, ice crusted surface - when you didn't hit the old stuff it skied very well! The lee aspects have been loaded in the last snowfall and we did not try our luck in them. Sunny, cold and windless all day in the alpine, (felt warm in the sun but was cold in the shade at treeline). The…

reports.title: Observation Forepeak
reports.comment: quick: Got a single whumph on a small alpine lee feature. Everything is wind-pressed as soon as you get out of the trees. We were able to find some sheltered deeper snow on the SW slope below Observation forepeak.

reports.title: West Nile Glades
reports.comment: snowpack: CTE 3 SP down 50 followed by CT 0 SP (failed while isolating the block) down 50. Sudden failure on the January 17th surface hoar layer. Location was at the top of treeline in a sheltered zone that recieved wind loading from both prevailing Westerly winds as well as Sunday's Northeasterly winds. Whumphing and cracking was observed in the localized area of the pit but elsewhere the snow wa…

reports.title: South dolomite
reports.comment:
quick: 5 to 10 cm yesterday (sunday) with some strong winds blowing north to south.  Plenty of drifting and scouring. Pockets of soft snow found with some wind crust as well that provided decent skiing and easy travel.
Of note there is  new sun crust from Saturday that is about 1 cm or so on south facing aspects. It is not supportive to a skier. Didn't dig to see what was above or below but it was…

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Skied the high ridge avalanche path at Helen Shoulder, looker's left of the burn area and then went out via the roadside glades. The path has a thin snowpack and I assume it went off or near ground at some point (early Jan storms?). Lots of rocks sticking out and old debris at the bottom. Under the most recent snow it was crusty, not the best skiing but still falling within the acceptable r…

reports.title: Cirque peak
reports.comment: quick: Temperature started out about -5C and we had a few awesome runs a treeline in calm, cool temps. A couple of hours from sunset the wind picked up and the temperature noticeably dropped. -19C and howling by the time we got back to the car. Full on storm shortly after that. Glad to get the last of the nice weather for the next few days!

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: avalanche: Through the day our ski group observed several large whumphs while traveling between 2050m and 2150m. While approaching the top of a gully feature BTL, a settlement occurred initiating a slab on the gully wall. SH was visible on the bed surface.

reports.title: Helen shoulder
reports.comment: quick: An inversion was present warm temperatures at higher elevations -2 and -1 while base was -30 according to thermometer. / avalanche: Group of 4. First person triged the slide lose dry snow. Slide was slow but had a long runout. The debris was also shallow under 50cm.

reports.title: Jimmy Junior Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Whumpfing only occured in an area of wind stiffened snow / avalanche: Avalanche was on south shoulder of Observation subpeak. We observed from across the valley. Tracks see, but we suspect remote skier triggered

reports.title: Observation Subpeak
reports.comment:
quick: CT22 - Pop 40cm down on hard crust
Elevation: 2300m
Slope aspect: SW
Slope angle: 20 degrees 
Snow depth: 105cm

Lots of wind effect and small slabs forming from high N/NE winds

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak and Glacier
reports.comment: quick: Skin up the shoulder was decent in the trees. Little signs of instability until just below treeline. Then the drums started drumming. Lots of drumming and lots of shooting cracks. Wind affect was widespread in the alpine and bootpacking was the best option. Even then kicking the sun affected wind crust was a little hard on the toes. No wind, bluebird until approaching the sub peak, there a …

reports.title: Bow Summit.
reports.comment: quick: Dug a pit at 2379m.  East facing just above Tree line.  Snow pack 120cm.  Ski penetration 20 cm; boot 50 cm.  30 deg slope.  Resistant planar at CTM 19 , 40 cm on crust layer. Fist to 25cm, 1 finger down another 15, 4 finger down another 10.  2nd crust 5cm thick at 85 cm.  We observed suffing on a shorter 40 degree slope in the shade (picture).  We observed a size 1 loose snow avalanche on …

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Nice afternoon tour into Jimmy Jr Bowl. No signs of instability or whumpfing but we observed a recent a size 1 loose snow avalanche in steep terrain.  Signs of surface hoar present.  Temps were manageable with inversion helping offset the frigid valley bottoms.  One other small party was in the area. Boot top silky pow, good stability and sweet views made for a great tour.

reports.title: Observation Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Skied SW aspect to 2300m (treeline). Avoided Alpine due to pronounced wind effect. Good skiing in sheltered areas treeline and below.

Surface hoar observed from bow parking to 2200m. Easy clean hand shear down to 30cm. At this elevation there was no overlying slab.

First extended column test at 2300m produced hard shear down 40cm on Jan17 suncrust and facets. No propagation noted. Second …

reports.title: Dolomite Circuit Highline Variation
reports.comment:
quick: Skied the Dolomite Circuit clockwise and took a highline route just below Dolomite Glacier instead of the traditional lowline route. We skied a short pitch from the ridge above Lake Katherine on our way as well.

The surface snow in the general area was pretty good, mostly powder over a firm (mostly) supportive wind slab. I was expecting to see more wind affected snow but outside of the usu…

reports.title: No tears to the onion
reports.comment:
quick: On our day tour to the onion we observed a recent size 2 avalanche under the headwall near bow hut, likely triggered by icefall. 

The glacier above bow hut consisted of facets over breakable crust which meant variable ski penetration (avg 15cm) and cautious skiing.  Snow depth was 250+.  Hand shears did produce results down ~40cm but this layer was not reactive with skinning or skiing. 

N…

reports.title: Ferris glacier
reports.comment: avalanche: Observed cornice failure triggering size 2 under the Onion

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Dug pits in the glades above the summer trail before reaching the slide path.  Two compression tests both yielded hard planar failures (25&27). Extended column test similarly failed (27) but did not propagate. Failures were all on crust layer 27cm deep. Height of snowpack was 120cm.  Depth hoar present at ground. 

Skied slide path first, crust layer was supportive for skiing and soft snow …

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: Found excellent powder on the east aspects at West Nile at treeline and below treeline.  Didn't not venture into the alpine but it looked like mixture of good skiing and wind slabs. In areas without much traffic just below treeline we had lots of whumpfing.

reports.title: Observation Peak
reports.comment: quick: Wind affected ski on observation peak - skied SW aspect up to 2500m.  Test pit at 2400m on 25 degree slope SW aspect -CTN.  ~5cm new snow on what looks to be a surface hoar layer. HS: 120cm - Air temp -16 at 12:00. Skiing was wind affected creating varied conditions from soft snow to wind slab.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Great Skiing in the crowfoot glades. No whumpfing or signs of cracks. Sluffing traveling fast and far on steep slopes / avalanche: 3  Na size 1.5 loose dry avalanches noticed in the ALP above the glades on 45 degree terrain.

reports.title: Mosquito Creek test pit vs Observations
reports.comment:
avalanche: Observation of natural avalanche on NE aspect from cornice failure / weather: Rapid increase in temperature throughout day / snowpack: CTH22 on decomposing facets below melt freeze crust. Light wind crust on surface. Storm snow 124-120 cm, F resistance. 
Snow particles, F resistance 120-105 cm.
Rounded particles 105-95 cm. 
Melt-freeze crust at 90 cm.
Decomposing facets 89-85 cm.
Decomp…

reports.title: Jimmy junior junior
reports.comment: weather: Rapid temp rise between 1030 and obs time. Likely strong inversion.

reports.title: Observation peak area
reports.comment: quick: Headed up towards Observation peak with the intention of skiing the N. Glacier, but turned around about 3/4 of the way up. While skiing was good at treeline and below on faceted snow, it quickly deteriorated above treeline to breakable crust and then very wind-affected hardpack in the alpine.

reports.title: Peyto Glacier
reports.comment: quick: ACC Jasper/Hinton Section Trip: 4 days on the N. end of Wapta Icefield. Climbed Mts. Baker, Rhondda & Olive. Approach via Peyto Lake, exit via Bow. No instabilities or recent avy activity observed (prev. WSl and LD to sz 2 obs.). Icefield heavily wind-affected. Avg. HS 230 on icefield; only 100cm at toe of Peyto Gl. Sunny but cold (T-low: -36C, T-high: -9C). Crampons were used on both Baker…

reports.title: Mt Baker. Cold.
reports.comment: quick: Made the summit of Mt Baker for sunset from Peyto Hut. Ski quality very bad. Wind blasted, wind slabs, wind crust, facets, pure junk. Cold AF. So cold. Views were unreal. Not a cloud in sight for 2 days straight! A bad day for skiing and summits, a great day for views, and we'll leave it at that. It was really cold. / weather: Cold and more cold. Endless views with perfect clarity, and extr…

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment:
quick: Skied east facing slopes to 2170m (treeline). Encountered windcrust in the alpine but good skiing below treeline. Significant faceting observed in dense forest. Noticed lose dry sluffing on steep terrain below rock bands. Sunny clear skies. 

Boot penetration 20cm
Ski penetration 5cm
Snow depth 210cm
Morning temp -25 afternoon temp -12

reports.title: Dolomite Sub Peak: Sluff step down
reports.comment: avalanche: Over confident in moderate rating in the alpine, even though snow was variable at best. Conscious and cautious of convex features. Sluff developed behind me, gained mass, stepped down in a small lee loaded pocket, sluff and slab debris caught up to me near the bottom. Saw the slab chunks at my feet moving slowly, pulled the JetForce not knowing if more was coming, Did not need it in the…

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment: quick: Lots of wind affect in the alpine on Cirque Forepeak, varying from hardback to punchy wind affected snow. Ski crampons would definitely be useful. Observed debris from two size 1 slab avalanches on S-ly aspects in alpine, at least a few days old. No other signs of instability noted. Tricky skiing in alpine, but great views!

reports.title: Flower Couloir
reports.comment: quick: Skied the Stem and Petal of Flower today. As expected the skiing was hard-breakable to boiler plate wind slabs in the alpine. Stem was in good condition for the boot pack, not so much for the way down. The same was observed in the petals, although there was an increase in the amount of facets underlying the wind slabs. In all alpine areas we experienced a 3-5cm wind slab/crust on top of fac…

reports.title: Snow Profile Bow Summit Study Plot
Crowfoot Mountain
reports.comment: quick: Made the summit of Crowfoot Mountain (and little crowfoot). Some fresh snow (about 10cm) made ski quality good. Seems that the snowfall was isolated a bit - since there was no fresh until about 6km in. I brought ski crampons but did not use them. The Bow Hut approach canyon is in fantastic shape. It was a super fast exit. No signs of instabilities noted during our day, saw a few recent loos…

reports.title: South dolomite shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Poked around the shoulder area. Very small pockets of good snow. Lots of variability in snow pack. Places with good snow had 20cm of sugar on top of a 5cm concrete wind/sum slab.

reports.title: A Sunny Day...and Some Touring
reports.comment: quick: It was beautifully warm and sunny... and that made it great. The area we skied today,  drainage and col to the North of cirque peak, had conditions more acurately described by the  "trace" snowfalls than the "20 cm" discussed in the avy bulletin. Without new snow to freshen things up, the area is a mixed bag for ski quality, hard, punchy, soft, crusty, facetted...etc.  We toured to the East…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Size 1.5 likely wind triggered point release of fresh loose dry on north facing Crowfoot forepeak to skiers left of Crowfoot Glades. See attached photo. / avalanche: Likely wind triggered point release of fresh loose dry slough on the Crowfoot forepeak to skiers left of Crowfoot Glades. No release of gully snow pack from impact of falling slough. See attached photo.

reports.title: COTR N.F, J.M, K.B, V.M
reports.comment: quick: Witnessed size two loose snow avalanche suspected natural trigger from cornice failure. / weather: Strong winds in the alpine carrying a lot of snow.

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak Avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: Reported mid afternoon March 15 : investigated March 16. Recent wind loading over previously highly wind effected and shallow slope. Continued wind loading was likely the trigger and some mild solar influence likely helped. Surface slab 30-50 deep stepped down another 40-50 to ground as two slabs failed in sympathy.

reports.title: Flower couloir, broken stem and dog leg
reports.comment: quick: Amazing conditions today up flower couloir and the upper petals to summit. Looks like the overnight freeze and clear skies helped facet the upper 20cm which made for amazing conditions (much better than Tuesday when we were also here). Bring crampons for the upper bowl.  Bit of sluffing on way  down but easily manageable. Skied down broken stem. Snow in sun was still -5’C in the sun at 12:3…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Toured over to Crowfoot glades Sunday April 7. Lake still has good coverage to cross. Snow on crowfoot glades was heavy powder. Riding quality was ok for April.

Did not observe any signs of instability while riding and touring. / weather: Snowed on and off all day with low to no wind. Periods of sun followed by flurries consistently through the day

reports.title: Jimmy Junior Peak
reports.comment: quick: Few (5-20 cm) powder on hard background, expected afternoon sun does not come. Upper slope has many pockets of snow that need to be avoided. Last steep slope bellow summit went down. Direct descent considered to be to risky. Lower part in trees, eastern slopes, gets reasonable corn, just right timing for descending.

reports.title: Jimmy Jr
reports.comment: avalanche: The avalanche in the picture was a natural that occurred around 11am. The winds were moderate from the west and this point release was on a east facing unsupported cliff ban. About an hour later we witnessed a solo skier trigger a size 2 slab near the summit of Jimmy jr. It propagated about 50m and ran about 200m. He was damn lucky to not get pulled into it. The clouds came in and I was…

reports.title: Crowfoot moraines skier remote sz 1.5
reports.comment: quick: While in the area, we witnessed a party of two remotely trigger a sz 1.5 slab avalanche from 50m away on a steep shaded North aspect face below a vertical head wall. 20-30cm crown (estimated), likely on facets.

reports.title: Dolomite Avalanch
reports.comment:
avalanche: Witnessed a large skier remote accidental avalanche off the east side of Dolomite shoulder this morning. 
Confirmed the current avalanche summary and conditions. 
Tucked tail and ran after watching this. 

https://youtu.be/GjFSVcZhvLs

reports.title: Bow hut region
reports.comment: quick: Supportive rain crust to bow hut which disappears above the hut on NE slopes below st nick. At higher elevation there is a thin wind slab on surface and beneath that about 30 cm of dry unconsolidated snow sitting on a well settled pack at this location. In wind exposed terrain and lee of ridge terrain in alpine this upper snow appears to have slabbed and we saw evidence of widespread slab a…

reports.title: Crowfoot Pass
reports.comment: weather: Toured up to Crowfoot Pass on Thursday 04/25. Early start at sunrise from Crowfoot Glacier VP. Traveling up to treeline was difficult on a strong MFcr, ski crampons would've been helpful/ were used. Above TL about 2 cm of light snow were sitting on a MFcr. Reached the pass by 11:30, T -3.7 °C, HS160, HST about 10, Wind M, SSE, PF about 15 cm. Obvious natural avalanche activity visible fro…

reports.title: Observation Peak
reports.comment: avalanche: Slope released 20 m below us while skiing down the main line up this side of Obs Peak. 20-40 cm slab on facets above a hard crust. Ran a surprisingly long distance. After skiing down we observed an adjacent size 2 avalanche with the same characteristics that had been remotely triggered by other skiers about 1 hour earlier.

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: Skied Little Crowfoot. Skiing across Bow Lake is still great and Bow canyon was still filled in.  There was some harder wind slabs in the high alpine but mostly skiable soft slab and powder below 2650m.  I needed to apply skin wax at 7:00am and scrape a few times but was better once we got in to the apline. Skiing was generally great!  We observed a few point release loose avalanches that d…
